discovery: Dynamical symmetries and supersymmetry in atomic nuclei (the Interacting Boson Model and its algebraic extensions)
motivation: Francesco Iachello introduced the Interacting Boson Model (with the late Akito Arima), showing that the collective spectra of heavy nuclei follow dynamical symmetries of the group U(6). Its three limits, U(5), SU(3) and O(6), unified vibrational, rotational and gamma-unstable nuclei within one algebraic framework and made precise, parameter-economical predictions for energies and electromagnetic transitions, confirmed across the nuclear chart. Iachello then proposed dynamical supersymmetry linking even-even, odd-A and odd-odd nuclei, a prediction confirmed by high-resolution spectroscopy of the 196Pt-197Au quartet. This was the first observation of supersymmetry realized in a physical system. He later introduced critical-point symmetries (E(5), X(5)) for shape phase transitions, also confirmed experimentally, and carried the algebraic method into molecular physics (the vibron model) and hadron spectroscopy. His work shows that abstract symmetry can organize complex many-body quantum systems and predict their behaviour, a lasting unifying idea across physics.
